name: Wisteria blue
lede: Wisteria Blue is a soft, periwinkle-leaning violet, a bluer modifier of the wisteria flower's family name, with no named sibling in our library closer than a light violet.

sections.title: A bluer wisteria
sections.body:
Our color library lists this hue under Ridgway's 1912 sources alongside the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 and the crowdsourced xkcd color survey of 2010, though none of them records a precise plate or hue number here [1]. It sits as a child of the "wisteria" family word, pulling the flower's usual soft purple further toward blue [1]; it also carries the older ISCC-NBS alternate name Light Bluish Violet [1].

Its nearest look-alike in our library is [[light-violet]], duller by a CIEDE2000 distance of 3.8, with [[deep-chicory-blue]] and [[periwinkle-blue]] not far behind [2]. Measured in LCH it is lightness 62, chroma 51 and hue 296 degrees, a fairly saturated blue-violet, notably more saturated than most named nature colors in this family [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this blue-violet in only 3 of 23,781 paintings (0.01%, as photographed), rarer than 79% of the named colors we track, making it one of the least-matched hues in the whole archive [3]. The only two dated matches run from 1905 to 1909, both by Albert Marquet [3]. In printed English the word pattern for "wisteria blue" peaks in the 1950s and rose fastest in the 1940s, decades after the ISCC-NBS and Ridgway records our library cites, so the color name likely spread later than its first listing [3].
